free_tier.stated: EUR 3.99/month for EPYC-01 in Eygelshoven, Netherlands: 1 vCore on an AMD EPYC with host CPU passthrough, 4 GB RAM, 50 GB NVMe, a routed IPv6 /64 plus one IPv4, unmetered traffic at 300 Mbit/s, no setup fee. EPYC-02 is EUR 7.99/month for 2 vCores, 8 GB and 100 GB at 600 Mbit/s; EPYC-03 is EUR 15.20 for 4 vCores, 16 GB and 150 GB at 1 Gbit/s; the range runs to EPYC-08 at EUR 53.90 for 12 vCores, 64 GB, 300 GB and a 10 Gbit/s port. Prices include VAT where it applies and are billed monthly in EUR.

egress.terms: unmetered, capped only by the plan port speed at the hypervisor NIC; no overage billing and no post-quota throttle

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
tooling: unusually well documented: a public REST API of 48 endpoints with scoped keys, a Discord bot for power actions, backups and firewall rules, an AGPL-3.0 control panel published at github.com/virtbase/virtbase, a public status page and a looking glass
chaining: EUR 3.99 for 4 GB with no identity document and no phone number is the cheapest route to a machine the client can actually register for, and the 48-endpoint API plus a Discord control plane makes it the one record here that a script can drive end to end without a browser 300 Mbit/s caps what it can serve, so it is a control node or a small worker and not a mirror

limits.value: traffic is unmetered by construction: the provider states the listed port speed is a hard rate limit applied at the hypervisor NIC, with no monthly volume allowance, no overage billing and no post-quota throttle. So 300 Mbit/s on the entry plan is the wall, and a byte counter is not. The 300 Mbit/s figure is also the reason the entry plan cannot be used to move terabytes quickly regardless of the unmetered term.

identity_cost.detail: no identity document, no phone number and no KYC at any stage, as stated by the provider in the offer post; card, PayPal and Stripe methods, plus Monero and Bitcoin on orders of EUR 5.00 or more

evidence.proved: the fetch returned upstream_status 403 with a provider-side snapshot of the page, which quotes: 'EPYC-01', 'EUR 3.99 per month', '1 vCore', '4GB RAM', '50GB NVMe SSD', '1 IPv4 + IPv6 /64 Subnet', '0.3Gb/s Uplink', 'Unlimited traffic', 'SkyLink Data Center, NL'; the same block pattern repeats through 'EPYC-08' at 'EUR 53.90 per month'

third-party offer post, published 2026-10-16, quoted from its table: 'EPYC-01 4 GB RAM 1 vCore AMD EPYC (host CPU passthrough) 50 GB NVMe SSD Unmetered traffic at 300 Mbit/s 1 x IPv4 + routed IPv6 /64 EUR 3.99/month'; provider quote: 'Traffic is unmetered: the listed port speed is a hard rate limit applied at the hypervisor NIC, so there is no monthly volume allowance, no overage billing and no post-quota throttle'; 'No KYC, no identity documents and no phone number at any point'

the post states the eligibility wall in its own numbered list: 'They can currently only bill customers in the EU-27. Their checkout and invoicing are wired for EU VAT only, so a US, UK, Swiss or Canadian buyer cannot complete an order today'

notes: Not in dossier/compute (searched: virtbase, no record). the plan figures quoted from it come from the provider-side snapshot the reader returned alongside the refusal, and they agree to the cent with the offer post's table, which is why the record is documented rather than reported.
